title: Pipeline profiling scratchpad — warmup penalty and distributed stalls
content:
Scratchpad: pipeline profiling — warmup penalty and distributed stalls

Context / goal:
- Trying to pin down the ~40-80ms first-token penalty we've been seeing on production hosted tier for medium bursts (10-30 qps) when requests go through the new http-proxy pool + router.
- Hypothesis: combination of (a) kernel hot-path not fully JIT'd until first long-latency request, (b) kv-cache hydration + prefix copying, and (c) router serialization during connection reuse. Need to instrument per-stage latencies.

Test harness / env:
- Model: open-llm/llama-2-13b-ggml-quant (serving-compat variant)
- Runtime: serving-runtime v1.14.2 (local debug build with RTT tracing flags)
- Hardware: g4dn.xlarge-like GPU equivalent (4 vCPU emulated), single-AZ demo cluster
- Sequence length: 256 prompt + up to 128 generated
- Batch sizes tested: 1, 2, 4 (concurrent requests), microbatch window 8ms, 16ms
- KV cache: enabled, cold at start for each worker; cache-shard strategy: per-worker prefix cache
- Proxy config: http-proxy v3, keepalive: 100 connections, max-concurrent-per-conn default
- Load generator: wrk2-like with scripted streaming (randomized prompt templates)
- Measurement: custom tracing that emits JSON lines for each request with stage timings: client-conn, proxy-queue, proxy-conn-setup, router-dispatch, worker-queue, worker-setup, kv-hydrate, first-token-gen, token-stream

Commands used:
- ./run_load.sh --qps 20 --concurrency 4 --seq 256 --model llm-13b --duration 300s --trace /tmp/traces.jsonl
- curl -v example: POST /v1/complete with X-Request-Id header to correlate traces

Raw-ish aggregated numbers (representative run 2025-11-08, qps=20, concurrency=4):
- Overall latency percentiles (ms): p50=92, p90=138, p95=210, p99=430
- First-token latency (ms): median_first=76, p90_first=122, p99_first=380
- Per-stage median breakdown (ms): client-conn=1, proxy-queue=6, proxy-conn-setup=2, router-dispatch=3, worker-queue=12, worker-setup=8, kv-hydrate=27, first-token-gen=39
- KV-cache hit-rate observed (worker-level): 0.63 (meaning ~37% cold or miss events)
- Tokens/sec overall: ~2300 tokens/s across cluster of 6 workers

Observations / interpretation:
1) First-token ~76ms median is split roughly between kv-hydrate (~27ms) and first-token-gen (~39ms). So both are meaningful contributors.
2) Worker-queue spikes correlate with proxy-queue spikes — when bursts appear, we see queueing at both proxy and worker sides; proxy-queue sometimes jumps to >45ms (rare) and seems to precede worker-queue increase.
3) Proxy connection churn: traces where proxy-conn-setup>10ms show higher downstream queuing. Not all requests re-use connections though. Keepalive isn't the only factor (some long-tail connections are GC'd).
4) KV cache warming: misses cost ~20-40ms depending on prefix copy size. Miss rate is tied to session affinity—requests for same API-key have much higher hit-rate.
5) Microbatching window length interacts with first-token latency: increasing microbatch window from 8ms->16ms lowers p99 tokens/s but slightly increases first-token by ~5-8ms due to batching delay. There's a tradeoff.

Quick experiments run and outcomes:
- A: disabled proxy (direct to router) => median_first down to 52ms, p99_first down to 200ms. Implication: proxy contributes ~20-30ms in median cases.
- B: pre-warm kv-cache for new workers (prefetch top-2 prefixes) => p50_first down by ~12ms, kv hit-rate up to 0.78. Works but costs memory and small cpu/network hit on worker start.
- C: jittered keepalive: tuned proxy keepalive timeout from 60s -> 300s; reduced conn-setup events but increased stale connections and occasional failures. Not ideal.
- D: increase microbatch window to 16ms => throughput improved 8%, but first-token median increased 6ms.

Hypotheses to test next (prioritized):
- H1: Router dispatch path has a hidden cost when request metadata is larger (function-calling vs simple text) — add additional size bucket tests.
- H2: KV hydrate cost scales with prefix length; run microbench copying 0,64,128,256 token prefixes to isolate copy cost.
- H3: TLS session resumption behavior between client-proxy-router-worker may add 8-12ms for some clients; capture TLS handshake counts.

Short-term mitigations recommended:
- Add an opportunistic kv-prefetch during worker warmup; tradeoff acceptable for dedicated pools. Ticket: PROJ-8871 linked above.
- Adjust default microbatch window to 10ms instead of 8ms for hosted tier with bursty traffic to slightly improve throughput without large first-token penalty.
- Instrument proxy to emit conn-reuse metric per-request and surface in console dashboards (need small telemetry change).

Open questions / notes to self:
- Do we have a clear mapping between session affinity keys and cache sharding? If not, recommendations could be wrong for multi-tenant workloads.
- How much does GC/heap-scan pause on worker affect first-token at low QPS? Need to correlate with node-level GC logs.
- For dedicated pools, pre-warm cost is acceptable; for hosted multi-tenant pools, it's trickier. Explore sampling-based prefetching.

Quick action items / TODOs:
- [ ] Run prefix-copy microbench (0/64/128/256) and produce clean chart (assigned: Priya)
- [ ] Add conn-reuse metric emit (assigned: Evan)
- [ ] Prototype worker prefetch hook on startup (small PoC, assigned: me)
- [ ] Write short runbook entry describing first-token troubleshooting steps (low effort)

Slack references:
- #serving-runtime: thread "first-token spike investigation" (Dec 1 2025) — see message thread id 4632 for example traces
- @infra-shared noted similar proxy churn on Nov 22 (ticket INF-2046)

Notes on presentation/graphs to produce for next sync:
- waterfall per-request showing stage timings for cold vs warm requests (overlay)
- KV miss-rate vs first-token latency scatter plot (points per minute)
- conn-reuse rate vs proxy-queue percentile chart (heatmap)

Closing quick summary (so I remember why I care):
- The ~40-80ms first-token penalty is multi-factor; KV hydration and proxy/conn churn are the two biggest levers.
- There are several feasible mitigations (prefetch, keepalive tuning, microbatch tuning), but they have tradeoffs that differ between hosted and dedicated pools.

End of scratchpad. Will iterate after Priya's microbench results and Evan's proxy metric PR.
